Martha Skelton, the attractive young widow whom Jefferson married in 1772, had many suitors before she settled on Jefferson. One day, according to a popular story, two gentlemen happened to call on her at the same time. They were friends and decided to go in together. But as they were about to pass from the hall into the drawing-room, they heard some music.

Someone was playing the violin, accompanied by the harpsichord, and a lady and a gentleman were singing. The two gentlemen knew at once who it was: Jefferson was the only violinist in the neighborhood.

They looked resignedly at each other.

"We are wasting our time," said one of them. "We may as well go home." So they donned their hats and left.

Source:

Boller, Paul F. "Thomas Jefferson." Presidential Anecdotes. New York: Oxford UP, 1981. 39, 40. Print.
